title: Grow the D5 fixture so the bench measures the costs D5 names: git ancestry, review candidates, transcript root
action: Panel BLOCKER repair (validation decision 2026-07-26): the pinned host-real fixture (crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs:126-169) carries only decisions/backlog/reservations/cells/onboarding/state/config and is deliberately built with no .git above it. On that fixture listCandidates returns empty, so buildReviewBlock (bee.mjs:409-433) loops ZERO times and spawns no git, and detectCrashCandidates (recovery.mjs:319-328) matches no encoded project dir so no transcript tail is read — meaning the D5 bench measures only the JSON-read third and misses BOTH costs D5 names (the ~97ms git derivation and the ~37ms transcript tail). GROW the generator so the fixture exercises them: (a) initialize a real git repo inside the fixture root with enough commits and refs that ancestry questions are genuine, while KEEPING root resolution correct (the fixture must still resolve as its own bee root — .bee/onboarding.json present; if a .git at the root breaks resolveRootsCore's first branch, place the git repo so both hold, and prove the resolved store root is the fixture in a test); (b) emit at least 60 review candidates plus review sessions with head/ref values that make deriveCandidateStatus do real work across all four statuses; (c) provide a transcript root the recovery block actually reads — inject it explicitly rather than depending on the developer's $HOME/.claude/projects, so the fixture is hermetic. Add new pinned floors for all three (candidate count, commit/ref count, transcript bytes) and REFUSE generation below them, exactly like the existing size floors. Update --self-test to assert the new floors and to assert NON-TRIVIALITY: on a generated fixture, `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs status --json` must report a non-zero review candidate total and a non-degraded review block — a fixture that still measures nothing is a failed generation, not a pass.

truths: queen-bench --self-test asserts every new floor and refuses generation below it

--self-test proves non-triviality on BOTH expensive blocks: bee.mjs status --json on a generated fixture reports a non-zero candidate total with a non-degraded review block AND a non-empty recovery/crash-candidate block (a transcript-bytes floor met by files detectCrashCandidates never matches is the same hollow-fixture failure one block over)
the generated fixture still resolves as its own bee root (asserted), and the transcript root is injected, not taken from the host $HOME
the existing size floors and refusal cases still hold

artifacts.substantive: fixture generator grown with git ancestry, review candidates/sessions, injected transcript root matching detectCrashCandidates' encoded-project-dir shape, new pinned floors

key_links: rust-port-14/20 use these fixtures as their git/transcript oracle roots
rust-port-15's bench and parity legs run on this grown fixture
prohibitions: No edits to .bee/bin/ or packages/bee/ (D1 freeze)
Never lower a floor to make generation succeed
The fixture never reads or writes the repo's live .bee/ store or the host $HOME
No edits to crates/Cargo.toml members list

verify: cargo build --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml && cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p queen-bench -- --self-test

trace.outcome: Grew queen-bench's D5 fixture generator to exercise the two status blocks the pinned-size-only fixture measured as zero: real git ancestry (>=50 commits + tags) co-located with .bee/ so root resolution still holds, a review-candidates ledger + 3 review sessions engineered to hit all four CANDIDATE_STATUSES, and one heartbeat-stale crash-candidate session with an injected (never /home/thanhsmind) transcript root matching detectCrashCandidates' encoded-project-dir layout. Added 3 new pinned floors (review candidates >=60, git commits >=50, transcript tail >=300KB) that --self-test refuses generation below (7/7 refusal cases), and a non-triviality assertion proving a real bee.mjs status --json read on the generated fixture reports non-zero, non-degraded review and recovery blocks.
